summary:
Orbit Mission Architect – Project Summary
Orbit Mission Architect is an interactive 3D space mission planning and visualization platform developed to make space mission design more accessible, understandable, and engaging. The platform allows users to explore mission specifications, visualize orbital profiles through 3D diagrams, and understand key aspects of spacecraft missions through an interactive Mission Architect interface.
It addresses the challenge by transforming complex space mission concepts into an intuitive visual experience, helping users better understand orbital paths, mission parameters, and space exploration planning. By combining interactive visualization with mission data, the platform bridges the gap between technical space science and practical learning.
This project is important because understanding orbital mechanics and mission architecture can be challenging for beginners and students. Orbit Mission Architect encourages curiosity, supports STEM education, and makes space exploration concepts easier to explore and communicate.
details: Orbit Mission Architect – Project Details Orbit Mission Architect is an interactive 3D space mission planning and visualization platform developed to make space mission concepts easier to understand and explore. What does it do and how does it work? The platform provides an interactive Mission Architect interface where users can inspect mission specifications, explore orbital profiles and visualize orbital concepts through 3D diagrams. It transforms complex space-related information into a more engaging visual experience. Benefits and intended impact: The project aims to make space science and orbital mechanics more approachable for students, beginners and space enthusiasts. It encourages STEM learning, curiosity and a better visual understanding of space mission concepts. Tools and technologies: The project was developed using JavaScript, React, Vite, HTML, CSS and Node.js. Visual Studio Code was used for development, GitHub for source-code management and Vercel for deployment. Creativity and innovation: The project combines interactive mission exploration with 3D orbital visualization in a single platform. Instead of relying only on static explanations, users can visually explore mission-related concepts. Factors considered: Our team focused on usability, visual clarity, accessibility, interactive learning and the potential to expand the platform with additional mission data and visualization capabilities.
